sanskrit: yūthānīva kiśorīṇāṃ sukeśīnāṃ janārdana snuṣāṇāṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrasya paśya vṛndāny anekaśaḥ
english: Like herds of young mares, O Janārdana, behold the many throngs of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's daughters-in-law, lovely-haired women gathered together.

sanskrit: ato duḥkhataraṃ kiṃ nu keśava pratibhāti me yad imāḥ kurvate sarvā rūpam uccāvacaṃ striyaḥ
english: What grief could seem more bitter to me than this, O Keśava — that all these women contort themselves into such wild and pitiful shapes?

sanskrit: nūnam ācaritaṃ pāpaṃ mayā pūrveṣu janmasu yā paśyāmi hatān putrān pautrān bhrātṝṃś ca keśava evam ārtā vilapatī dadarśa nihataṃ sutam
english: Surely some sin was done by me in former births, that I now look upon my slain sons, grandsons, and brothers, O Keśava. — Thus lamenting in her anguish, she beheld her own slain son.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato duryodhanaṃ dṛṣṭvā gāndhārī śokakarśitā sahasā nyapatad bhūmau chinneva kadalī vane
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, beholding Duryodhana, Gāndhārī, wasted with grief, fell suddenly to the earth like a plantain tree cut down in the forest.

sanskrit: sā tu labdhvā punaḥ saṃjñāṃ vikruśya ca punaḥ punaḥ duryodhanam abhiprekṣya śayānaṃ rudhirokṣitam
english: But regaining her senses, and crying out again and again, she gazed upon Duryodhana lying there drenched in blood.

sanskrit: pariṣvajya ca gāndhārī kṛpaṇaṃ paryadevayat hā hā putreti śokārtā vilalāpākulendriyā
english: And embracing him, Gāndhārī lamented piteously: 'Alas, alas, my son!' — wailing thus, stricken with grief, her senses overwhelmed.

sanskrit: sugūḍhajatru vipulaṃ hāraniṣkaniṣevitam vāriṇā netrajenoraḥ siñcantī śokatāpitā samīpasthaṃ hṛṣīkeśam idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Drenching with tears born of her eyes his broad chest with its well-hidden collarbones, adorned with necklaces and golden ornaments, and burning with sorrow, she spoke these words to Hṛṣīkeśa, who stood near at hand:

sanskrit: upasthite 'smin saṃgrāme jñātīnāṃ saṃkṣaye vibho mām ayaṃ prāha vārṣṇeya prāñjalir nṛpasattamaḥ asmiñ jñātisamuddharṣe jayam ambā bravītu me
english: When this battle, the destruction of our kinsmen, was at hand, O mighty one, this best of kings, O scion of Vṛṣṇi, said to me with folded hands: 'In this clash of kinsmen, let my mother foretell me victory.'

sanskrit: ity ukte jānatī sarvam ahaṃ svaṃ vyasanāgamam abruvaṃ puruṣavyāghra yato dharmas tato jayaḥ
english: When he had spoken thus, knowing well the whole coming of my ruin, I said, O tiger among men: 'Where righteousness is, there is victory.'

sanskrit: yathā na yudhyamānas tvaṃ saṃpramuhyasi putraka dhruvaṃ śastrajitāṃl lokān prāptāsy amaravad vibho
english: 'Inasmuch as you do not falter while you fight, my son, surely you shall attain the worlds won by the sword, and dwell there like an immortal, O lord.'

sanskrit: ity evam abruvaṃ pūrvaṃ nainaṃ śocāmi vai prabho dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ tu śocāmi kṛpaṇaṃ hatabāndhavam
english: Thus did I speak to him before; therefore I do not grieve for him, O lord. But I grieve for Dhṛtarāṣṭra, wretched and bereft of his kinsmen.

sanskrit: amarṣaṇaṃ yudhāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ kṛtāstraṃ yuddhadurmadam śayānaṃ vīraśayane paśya mādhava me sutam
english: Behold my son, O Mādhava — unyielding, the foremost of warriors, skilled in arms, fierce in battle — now lying upon the hero's bed.

sanskrit: yo 'yaṃ mūrdhāvasiktānām agre yāti paraṃtapaḥ so 'yaṃ pāṃsuṣu śete 'dya paśya kālasya paryayam
english: He who marched at the head of consecrated kings, the scorcher of foes — he now lies today in the dust. Behold the turning of time!

sanskrit: dhruvaṃ duryodhano vīro gatiṃ nasulabhāṃ gataḥ tathā hy abhimukhaḥ śete śayane vīrasevite
english: Surely the hero Duryodhana has gone to a state not easily won, for he lies thus facing forward upon the bed that heroes share.

sanskrit: yaṃ purā paryupāsīnā ramayanti mahīkṣitaḥ mahītalasthaṃ nihataṃ gṛdhrās taṃ paryupāsate
english: He whom kings once attended and delighted as they sat about him — him, now slain and lying upon the earth, the vultures attend.

sanskrit: yaṃ purā vyajanair agryair upavījanti yoṣitaḥ tam adya pakṣavyajanair upavījanti pakṣiṇaḥ
english: He whom women once fanned with the finest fans — him today the birds fan with their wings.

sanskrit: eṣa śete mahābāhur balavān satyavikramaḥ siṃheneva dvipaḥ saṃkhye bhīmasenena pātitaḥ
english: Here lies the mighty-armed one, strong and of true valor, struck down in battle by Bhīmasena as an elephant by a lion.

sanskrit: paśya duryodhanaṃ kṛṣṇa śayānaṃ rudhirokṣitam nihataṃ bhīmasenena gadām udyamya bhārata
english: Behold Duryodhana, O Kṛṣṇa, lying drenched in blood, slain by Bhīmasena who raised high his mace, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: akṣauhiṇīr mahābāhur daśa caikāṃ ca keśava anayad yaḥ purā saṃkhye so 'nayān nidhanaṃ gataḥ
english: He, the mighty-armed, who once led eleven full armies into battle, O Keśava — that very leader has now gone to his death.

sanskrit: eṣa duryodhanaḥ śete maheṣvāso mahārathaḥ śārdūla iva siṃhena bhīmasenena pātitaḥ
english: Here lies Duryodhana, the great archer, the mighty chariot-warrior, struck down by Bhīmasena as a tiger by a lion.

sanskrit: viduraṃ hy avamanyaiṣa pitaraṃ caiva mandabhāk bālo vṛddhāvamānena mando mṛtyuvaśaṃ gataḥ
english: For this ill-fated one, scorning Vidura and his own father — a foolish boy, through his contempt for his elders — has, in his folly, fallen under the power of death.

sanskrit: niḥsapatnā mahī yasya trayodaśa samāḥ sthitā sa śete nihato bhūmau putro me pṛthivīpatiḥ
english: He whose dominion over the earth stood unrivaled for thirteen years — my son, the lord of the earth, now lies slain upon the ground.

sanskrit: apaśyaṃ kṛṣṇa pṛthivīṃ dhārtarāṣṭrānuśāsanāt pūrṇāṃ hastigavāśvasya vārṣṇeya na tu tac ciram
english: I once beheld the earth, O Kṛṣṇa, under the rule of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son, full of elephants, cattle, and horses, O scion of Vṛṣṇi — but that did not last long.

sanskrit: tām evādya mahābāho paśyāmy anyānuśāsanāt hīnāṃ hastigavāśvena kiṃ nu jīvāmi mādhava
english: That same earth today, O mighty-armed one, I see under another's rule, stripped of elephants, cattle, and horses. Why, then, should I go on living, O Mādhava?

sanskrit: idaṃ kṛcchrataraṃ paśya putrasyāpi vadhān mama yad imāḥ paryupāsante hatāñ śūrān raṇe striyaḥ
english: Behold this, more grievous even than the slaying of my son: that these women sit beside the heroes slain in battle.

sanskrit: prakīrṇakeśāṃ suśroṇīṃ duryodhanabhujāṅkagām rukmavedīnibhāṃ paśya kṛṣṇa lakṣmaṇamātaram
english: Behold, O Kṛṣṇa, the mother of Lakṣmaṇa — her hair disheveled, fair of hip, lying in the cradle of Duryodhana's arm, radiant as a golden altar.

sanskrit: nūnam eṣā purā bālā jīvamāne mahābhuje bhujāv āśritya ramate subhujasya manasvinī
english: Surely this young and spirited woman, while the mighty-armed one yet lived, would once take delight resting upon the arms of him whose arms were so fair.

sanskrit: kathaṃ tu śatadhā nedaṃ hṛdayaṃ mama dīryate paśyantyā nihataṃ putraṃ putreṇa sahitaṃ raṇe
english: How is it that this heart of mine does not shatter into a hundred pieces, as I look upon my slain son together with his own son in the field of battle?

sanskrit: putraṃ rudhirasaṃsiktam upajighraty aninditā duryodhanaṃ tu vāmorūḥ pāṇinā parimārjati
english: The blameless woman of lovely thighs kisses her son drenched in blood, and with her hand she wipes clean Duryodhana's body.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu śocati bhartāraṃ putraṃ caiṣā manasvinī tathā hy avasthitā bhāti putraṃ cāpy abhivīkṣya sā
english: Does this spirited woman grieve for her husband or for her son? For so she appears, set thus between them, even as she gazes upon her son as well.

sanskrit: svaśiraḥ pañcaśākhābhyām abhihatyāyatekṣaṇā pataty urasi vīrasya kururājasya mādhava
english: The long-eyed one strikes her own head with both her five-branched hands, then falls upon the breast of the hero, the king of the Kurus, O Mādhava.

sanskrit: puṇḍarīkanibhā bhāti puṇḍarīkāntaraprabhā mukhaṃ vimṛjya putrasya bhartuś caiva tapasvinī
english: Fair as a lotus, with the inner glow of a lotus, the suffering woman shines as she wipes clean the face of her son and of her husband.

sanskrit: yadi cāpy āgamāḥ santi yadi vā śrutayas tathā dhruvaṃ lokān avāpto 'yaṃ nṛpo bāhubalārjitān
english: If the sacred traditions are true, and if the scriptures speak truly, then surely this king has attained the worlds won by the strength of his arms.

sanskrit: gāndhāry uvāca paśya mādhava putrān me śatasaṃkhyāñ jitaklamān gadayā bhīmasenena bhūyiṣṭhaṃ nihatān raṇe
english: Gāndhārī said: Behold, O Mādhava, my sons, a hundred in number, who conquered fatigue — most of them slain in battle by Bhīmasena's mace.

sanskrit: idaṃ duḥkhataraṃ me 'dya yad imā muktamūrdhajāḥ hataputrā raṇe bālāḥ paridhāvanti me snuṣāḥ
english: This is more bitter to me today: that these young daughters-in-law of mine, their hair loosened, their sons slain in battle, run about distraught.

sanskrit: prāsādatalacāriṇyaś caraṇair bhūṣaṇānvitaiḥ āpannā yat spṛśantīmā rudhirārdrāṃ vasuṃdharām
english: They who once walked upon palace terraces, with feet adorned with ornaments, have come to this — that now they tread the blood-soaked earth.

sanskrit: gṛdhrān utsārayantyaś ca gomāyūn vāyasāṃs tathā śokenārtā vighūrṇantyo mattā iva caranty uta
english: Driving off the vultures, the jackals, and the crows, stricken with grief and reeling, they wander about as though drunk.

sanskrit: eṣānyā tv anavadyāṅgī karasaṃmitamadhyamā ghoraṃ tad vaiśasaṃ dṛṣṭvā nipataty atiduḥkhitā
english: And this other, faultless of body, her waist no wider than a hand's span, beholding that dreadful slaughter, falls down overcome with grief.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā me pārthivasutām etāṃ lakṣmaṇamātaram rājaputrīṃ mahābāho mano na vyupaśāmyati
english: Seeing this princess, the mother of Lakṣmaṇa, daughter of a king, O mighty-armed one, my mind finds no peace.

sanskrit: bhrātṝṃś cānyāḥ patīṃś cānyāḥ putrāṃś ca nihatān bhuvi dṛṣṭvā paripatanty etāḥ pragṛhya subhujā bhujān
english: Some, beholding their brothers slain upon the ground, and others their husbands, and others their sons, these fair-armed women fall down, clasping their dead in their arms.

sanskrit: madhyamānāṃ tu nārīṇāṃ vṛddhānāṃ cāparājita ākrandaṃ hatabandhūnāṃ dāruṇe vaiśase śṛṇu
english: Hear, O unconquered one, the wailing of the women of middle years and of the aged, bereft of their kinsmen, amid this terrible carnage.

sanskrit: rathanīḍāni dehāṃś ca hatānāṃ gajavājinām āśritāḥ śramamohārtāḥ sthitāḥ paśya mahābala
english: Behold, O mighty one, how they stand leaning upon the chariot-frames and the bodies of slain elephants and horses, worn out and faint with exhaustion.

sanskrit: anyā cāpahṛtaṃ kāyāc cārukuṇḍalam unnasam svasya bandhoḥ śiraḥ kṛṣṇa gṛhītvā paśya tiṣṭhati
english: And behold, O Kṛṣṇa, another stands holding the head of her own kinsman, severed from the body — fair with its earrings, high of nose.

sanskrit: pūrvajātikṛtaṃ pāpaṃ manye nālpam ivānagha etābhir anavadyābhir mayā caivālpamedhayā
english: No small sin, I think, was done in a former life, O sinless one, by these blameless women and by me of feeble wit.

sanskrit: tad idaṃ dharmarājena yātitaṃ no janārdana na hi nāśo 'sti vārṣṇeya karmaṇoḥ śubhapāpayoḥ
english: This requital has been visited upon us through the King of Righteousness, O Janārdana; for there is no perishing, O scion of Vṛṣṇi, of deeds, whether good or evil.

sanskrit: pratyagravayasaḥ paśya darśanīyakucodarāḥ kuleṣu jātā hrīmatyaḥ kṛṣṇapakṣākṣimūrdhajāḥ
english: Behold these women in the first bloom of youth, fair of breast and belly, born in noble families, full of modesty, with dark eyes, dark lashes, and dark hair.

sanskrit: haṃsagadgadabhāṣiṇyo duḥkhaśokapramohitāḥ sārasya iva vāśantyaḥ patitāḥ paśya mādhava
english: Behold, O Mādhava, how, their voices once soft and faltering as a swan's, now bewildered by pain and grief, they have fallen down, crying out like cranes.

sanskrit: phullapadmaprakāśāni puṇḍarīkākṣa yoṣitām anavadyāni vaktrāṇi tapaty asukharaśmivān
english: The blameless faces of these women, bright as full-blown lotuses, O lotus-eyed one — the sun, with its rays now bringing only sorrow, scorches them.

sanskrit: īrṣūṇāṃ mama putrāṇāṃ vāsudevāvarodhanam mattamātaṅgadarpāṇāṃ paśyanty adya pṛthagjanāḥ
english: The harem of my jealous sons, proud as rutting elephants and guarded close, O Vāsudeva, common men now gaze upon today.

sanskrit: śatacandrāṇi carmāṇi dhvajāṃś cādityasaṃnibhān raukmāṇi caiva varmāṇi niṣkān api ca kāñcanān
english: Their shields blazoned with a hundred moons, their banners radiant as the sun, their golden coats of mail, and their golden ornaments —

sanskrit: śīrṣatrāṇāni caitāni putrāṇāṃ me mahītale paśya dīptāni govinda pāvakān suhutān iva
english: and these helmets of my sons upon the ground — behold them, O Govinda, blazing like well-fed sacrificial fires.

sanskrit: eṣa duḥśāsanaḥ śete śūreṇāmitraghātinā pītaśoṇitasarvāṅgo bhīmasenena pātitaḥ
english: Here lies Duḥśāsana, his every limb drained of blood, struck down by the valiant Bhīmasena, slayer of foes.

sanskrit: gadayā vīraghātinyā paśya mādhava me sutam dyūtakleśān anusmṛtya draupadyā coditena ca
english: Behold my son, O Mādhava, slain by that hero-slaying mace — by Bhīma, who remembered the torments of the dice and was spurred on by Draupadī.

sanskrit: uktā hy anena pāñcālī sabhāyāṃ dyūtanirjitā priyaṃ cikīrṣatā bhrātuḥ karṇasya ca janārdana
english: For by this man was Pāñcālī addressed in the assembly hall, when she had been won at dice — by one wishing to please his brother and Karṇa, O Janārdana:

sanskrit: sahaiva sahadevena nakulenārjunena ca dāsabhāryāsi pāñcāli kṣipraṃ praviśa no gṛhān
english: 'Together with Sahadeva, with Nakula, and with Arjuna, you are the wife of slaves, O Pāñcālī; enter our house at once.'

sanskrit: tato 'ham abruvaṃ kṛṣṇa tadā duryodhanaṃ nṛpam mṛtyupāśaparikṣiptaṃ śakuniṃ putra varjaya
english: Then I said, O Kṛṣṇa, to King Duryodhana, ensnared in the noose of death: 'My son, forsake Śakuni.'

sanskrit: nibodhainaṃ sudurbuddhiṃ mātulaṃ kalahapriyam kṣipram enaṃ parityajya putra śāmyasva pāṇḍavaiḥ
english: 'Know this uncle of yours for a man of evil counsel, a lover of strife. Cast him off at once, my son, and make peace with the Pāṇḍavas.'

sanskrit: na budhyase tvaṃ durbuddhe bhīmasenam amarṣaṇam vāṅnārācais tudaṃs tīkṣṇair ulkābhir iva kuñjaram
english: 'You do not understand, O foolish one, the unforgiving Bhīmasena, whom you goad with sharp arrows of words as one torments an elephant with firebrands.'

sanskrit: tān eṣa rabhasaḥ krūro vākśalyān avadhārayan utsasarja viṣaṃ teṣu sarpo govṛṣabheṣv iva
english: But he, fierce and cruel, holding fast to those barbs of speech, poured out his venom upon them, as a serpent upon cattle.

sanskrit: eṣa duḥśāsanaḥ śete vikṣipya vipulau bhujau nihato bhīmasenena siṃheneva maharṣabhaḥ
english: Here lies Duḥśāsana, his two broad arms flung wide, slain by Bhīmasena as a great bull by a lion.

sanskrit: atyartham akarod raudraṃ bhīmaseno 'tyamarṣaṇaḥ duḥśāsanasya yat kruddho 'pibac choṇitam āhave
english: Bhīmasena, exceedingly unforgiving, wrought a deed most savage: that, enraged, he drank the blood of Duḥśāsana in battle.

sanskrit: gāndhāry uvāca eṣa mādhava putro me vikarṇaḥ prājñasaṃmataḥ bhūmau vinihataḥ śete bhīmena śatadhā kṛtaḥ
english: Gāndhārī said: Here, O Mādhava, my son Vikarṇa, honored by the wise, lies slain upon the ground, hewn into a hundred pieces by Bhīma.

sanskrit: gajamadhyagataḥ śete vikarṇo madhusūdana nīlameghaparikṣiptaḥ śaradīva divākaraḥ
english: Vikarṇa lies amid the elephants, O slayer of Madhu, like the autumn sun encircled by a dark cloud.

sanskrit: asya cāpagraheṇaiṣa pāṇiḥ kṛtakiṇo mahān kathaṃ cic chidyate gṛdhrair attukāmais talatravān
english: This great hand of his, calloused from gripping the bow and still wearing its leather guard, the vultures, eager to devour it, can scarcely tear apart.

sanskrit: asya bhāryāmiṣaprepsūn gṛdhrān etāṃs tapasvinī vārayaty aniśaṃ bālā na ca śaknoti mādhava
english: His young wife, the poor suffering girl, ceaselessly drives off these vultures that hunger for his flesh, yet she cannot prevail, O Mādhava.

sanskrit: yuvā vṛndārakaḥ śūro vikarṇaḥ puruṣarṣabha sukhocitaḥ sukhārhaś ca śete pāṃsuṣu mādhava
english: Young, noble, and valiant, Vikarṇa, a bull among men, accustomed to comfort and deserving of comfort, now lies in the dust, O Mādhava.

sanskrit: karṇinālīkanārācair bhinnamarmāṇam āhave adyāpi na jahāty enaṃ lakṣmīr bharatasattamam
english: Though his vital points were pierced in battle by barbed shafts, reed-arrows, and iron darts, even now beauty does not forsake him, this best of Bharata's line.

sanskrit: eṣa saṃgrāmaśūreṇa pratijñāṃ pālayiṣyatā durmukho 'bhimukhaḥ śete hato 'rigaṇahā raṇe
english: Here lies Durmukha, slayer of hosts of foes, slain in battle as he faced the foe — struck down by a hero of the field who was keeping his vow.

sanskrit: tasyaitad vadanaṃ kṛṣṇa śvāpadair ardhabhakṣitam vibhāty abhyadhikaṃ tāta saptamyām iva candramāḥ
english: This face of his, O Kṛṣṇa, half-devoured by beasts of prey, yet shines all the more, my dear, like the moon on the seventh night.

sanskrit: śūrasya hi raṇe kṛṣṇa yasyānanam athedṛśam sa kathaṃ nihato 'mitraiḥ pāṃsūn grasati me sutaḥ
english: A hero whose face in battle was such as this, O Kṛṣṇa — how could my son have been slain by his enemies, and now lies devouring the dust?

sanskrit: yasyāhavamukhe saumya sthātā naivopapadyate sa kathaṃ durmukho 'mitrair hato vibudhalokajit
english: He against whom, O gentle one, none could stand firm at the forefront of battle — how was Durmukha, who could win the world of the gods, slain by his foes?

sanskrit: citrasenaṃ hataṃ bhūmau śayānaṃ madhusūdana dhārtarāṣṭram imaṃ paśya pratimānaṃ danuṣmatām
english: Behold this son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Citrasena, slain and lying upon the ground, O slayer of Madhu — he who was the very measure of all bowmen.

sanskrit: taṃ citramālyābharaṇaṃ yuvatyaḥ śokakarśitāḥ kravyādasaṃghaiḥ sahitā rudantyaḥ paryupāsate
english: Him, with his bright garlands and ornaments, young women wasted with grief attend, weeping, together with the gathered beasts of prey.

sanskrit: strīṇāṃ ruditanirghoṣaḥ śvāpadānāṃ ca garjitam citrarūpam idaṃ kṛṣṇa vicitraṃ pratibhāti me
english: The wailing of the women and the howling of the wild beasts — this strange spectacle, O Kṛṣṇa, appears to me wondrous and terrible.

sanskrit: yuvā vṛndārako nityaṃ pravarastrīniṣevitaḥ viviṃśatir asau śete dhvastaḥ pāṃsuṣu mādhava
english: That Viviṃśati, young and noble, ever attended by the loveliest of women, now lies cast down in the dust, O Mādhava.

sanskrit: śarasaṃkṛttavarmāṇaṃ vīraṃ viśasane hatam parivāryāsate gṛdhrāḥ pariviṃśā viviṃśatim
english: Vultures, a score and more, sit ringed about the hero Viviṃśati, his armor shredded by arrows, slain in the carnage.

sanskrit: praviśya samare vīraḥ pāṇḍavānām anīkinīm āviśya śayane śete punaḥ satpuruṣocitam
english: The hero, having charged into the army of the Pāṇḍavas in battle, lies now upon the bed that befits a man of valor.

sanskrit: smitopapannaṃ sunasaṃ subhru tārādhipopamam atīva śubhraṃ vadanaṃ paśya kṛṣṇa viviṃśateḥ
english: Behold, O Kṛṣṇa, the exceedingly fair face of Viviṃśati — graced with a smile, finely nosed, fair of brow, like the lord of stars, the moon.

sanskrit: yaṃ sma taṃ paryupāsante vasuṃ vāsavayoṣitaḥ krīḍantam iva gandharvaṃ devakanyāḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: He whom the women of Vāsava once attended like a Vasu, even as celestial maidens by the thousand attend a sporting gandharva —

sanskrit: hantāraṃ vīrasenānāṃ śūraṃ samitiśobhanam nibarhaṇam amitrāṇāṃ duḥsahaṃ viṣaheta kaḥ
english: the slayer of heroic armies, the valiant one, resplendent in the assembly of war, the destroyer of foes — who could have withstood this unbearable warrior?
